question: The Gwalior Fort was initiated by ______ who finished the fortification system around the plateau in 773 CE.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Sourya Sena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Gwalior Fort** is one of the most significant and historic forts in India, located in **Madhya Pradesh**. It is renowned for its architectural brilliance and historical importance.
 
• The fort was initiated by **Raja Sourya Sena** in **773 CE**. He is credited with laying the foundations of this architectural marvel and establishing its fortification system. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• The Gwalior Fort is situated on a **steep sandstone plateau** and has witnessed various rulers and dynasties over the centuries, adding to its rich history and heritage.
 
• Raja Sourya Sena was a ruler who contributed significantly to the early development and defense of the region through this fortification, ensuring the security of his kingdom.
 
• Over time, the fort came under the control of several dynasties, including the **Tomars, Mughals, Marathas, and British**, each leaving their mark on the fort's architecture and history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Architectural Features:**

 
 
• The fort comprises several **palaces, temples, and water tanks**, demonstrating a blend of various architectural styles from different eras.
 
• One of the most famous structures within the fort is the **Man Singh Palace**, built by Tomar king Man Singh in the 15th century. It is renowned for its intricate artwork and tile work.
 
• The **Saas-Bahu Temple** and the **Teli Ka Mandir** are other notable landmarks within the fort, showcasing unique architectural styles.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Gwalior Fort has been a site of numerous battles and power struggles, reflecting the turbulent history of the region.
 
• It was a strategic stronghold due to its location and fortifications, making it a coveted possession for many rulers.
 
• During the Mughal era, the fort served as a prison for political prisoners and royalty.
 
 
 
• **Tourist Attraction:**
 
 
• Today, the Gwalior Fort is a popular tourist destination and is often referred to as the “**Gibraltar of India**” due to its impressive structure and historical significance.
 
• The fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding city and is a UNESCO-recognized monument, attracting history enthusiasts and architecture lovers alike.
 
 
 
• **Other Dynasties:**
 
 
• The fort was later ruled by the **Tomar dynasty**, under whom it saw significant architectural developments.
 
• It also came under the control of the Mughals, particularly during the reign of Babur and Akbar.
 
• The Marathas and later the British also controlled the fort, each adding their own influence to its history.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Akbar:**

 
 
• **Mughal emperor Akbar** captured the Gwalior Fort in the 16th century. However, he was not responsible for its initiation or original construction.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga:**
 
 
• **Rana Sanga**, the Rajput ruler of Mewar, was a significant historical figure known for his resistance against the Mughals but had no direct association with the construction of the Gwalior Fort.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• **Ashoka the Great**, the Mauryan emperor, is renowned for his contribution to spreading Buddhism and his edicts, but he was not connected to the Gwalior Fort.
